instruction: Chrome keeps prompting me to save passwords and I find it annoying. I want to turn off the password manager feature. Can you show me how?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y
cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"profile":{"password_manager_enabled": true}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to disable the password manager feature in Chrome. The evaluator checks that password_manager_enabled in profile settings is set to false. Verified by analyzing Chrome preferences profile settings.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator correctly verifies the single requirement (disable password manager by checking password_manager_enabled == false)
Getter logic correct: Extracts password_manager_enabled from profile.password_manager_enabled in Chrome Preferences file at OS-specific correct locations
Metric comparison correct: Uses boolean equality comparison (result_state == expected_value) which is semantically appropriate
Expected value correct: false semantically represents disabled state as required by instruction

Parameter handling correct: Metric correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule' - directly accesses expected_state.get('expected_value') instead of incorrect patterns like expected.get('rules')
Data flow correct: Getter returns boolean -> Metric compares boolean -> Semantically compatible types
State accessibility: Getter reads from disk file (Chrome Preferences JSON), not transient UI state, so verification is reliable
Postconfig appropriate: Restarts Chrome to ensure Preferences file is written to disk and can be read by getter
Cross-platform support: Handles Windows/macOS/Linux path differences correctly
Error handling: Has try/except with reasonable default (True = enabled by default in Chrome)
